items.claim: The row's boundary is warranted by tier-1 signals on both edges: a fresh imperative addressee-shift opens it and a closing self-declaration precedes the next koh-amar frame, and it correctly declines to name the unnamed servant referent.
items.evidence: The unit opens on the fresh addressee-shift “Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.” (web:Isa.43.8), moves through the nations-summons and witness-verdict formula “You are my witnesses,” says Yahweh (web:Isa.43.10, byte tier at אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה), and closes at “Yes, since the day was, I am he… I will work, and who can hinder it?” (web:Isa.43.13), immediately before the fresh title-stacked koh-amar frame that opens the next verse. The unnamed 'my servant' at Isa.43.10 sits among the book's unresolved servant-figure sites rather than its named-referent class, and the row correctly leaves that referent undecided. Both span-relevant setumah marks (Isa.43.10, Isa.43.13) are symmetrically disclosed as single-witness.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah single-witness (setumah marks, Isa.43.10 and Isa.43.13)

items.claim: The two-verse unit is fully bracketed by tier-1 divine-speech frames: a fresh title-stacked koh-amar opens it and a second fresh koh-amar closes it, so despite a real single-complex merge rival the row's narrower cut has its own complete warrant.
items.evidence: The Redeemer/Holy-One title stack opens the unit at “Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says:” (web:Isa.43.14, byte tier at כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל), a different divine-title pairing than the bare self-declaration of the row before it, and the announcement closes two verses later at “I am Yahweh, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.” (web:Isa.43.15), immediately before the second fresh koh-amar frame opens the following verse. The span-relevant setumah mark at Isa.43.15 is disclosed.

items.claim: The koh-amar messenger formula that opens the unit governs a chain of participles describing Yahweh across the next verse, so the imperative new-thing turn that follows is the content the formula introduces rather than an independent onset, and the row discloses that internal move honestly rather than over-cutting it.
items.evidence: A fresh koh-amar opens the unit at “Yahweh, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters,” (web:Isa.43.16, byte tier at כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ); the participles naming Yahweh's exodus-acts (byte tier: הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן ... הַמּוֹצִ֥יא) continue as the grammatical subject description governed by that same koh-amar verb through Isa.43.17, before the imperative turn “Don't remember the former things… Behold, I will do a new thing.” (web:Isa.43.18-Isa.43.19) begins the quoted speech proper; the unit runs to its purpose-clause close “that they might declare my praise.” (web:Isa.43.21), just ahead of the address reversal that opens the next row. The internal participle-to-imperative move is disclosed as the rejected alternative rather than silently absorbed.

items.claim: The row's boundaries are warranted by a genuine addressee reversal opening the unit and a verdict formula closing it, matching the book's own trial-speech pattern for this exact span.
items.evidence: The address reverses from the preceding oracle's third-person self-predication to direct accusation at “Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; but you have been weary of me, Israel.” (web:Isa.43.22, byte tier at וְלֹא אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב), running through the legal-dispute imperative “Let us plead together. Declare your case, that you may be justified.” (web:Isa.43.26) to the judgment-verdict close “I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.” (web:Isa.43.28), immediately before the fresh fear-not address to Jacob and Israel opens the next row. All three span-relevant setumah marks (Isa.43.21 neighbor, Isa.43.24, Isa.43.28) are symmetrically disclosed.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah single-witness (setumah marks, Isa.43.24 and Isa.43.28)

items.claim: The unit is warranted by a fresh fear-not/koh-amar frame reopening after the preceding lawsuit's verdict, and Jacob/Israel are correctly read in the named-referent servant class rather than the unresolved zones.
items.evidence: The row opens on a sharp comfort-after-judgment reversal, “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1, byte tier at וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י), restating the fear-not pattern of Isa.43.1 inside a fresh koh-amar frame at Isa.44.2, and closes on the naming formula “honor the name of Israel.” (web:Isa.44.5), just ahead of the royal self-declaration opening Isa.44.6. Jacob and Israel are named as servant here, correctly placed in the book's named-referent class rather than its held-open zones. The petuchah mark at Isa.44.5 is disclosed.

items.claim: The unit is warranted by a fresh royal-and-Redeemer koh-amar frame opening it and a rock-epithet closing it before the register shift to third-person satire, and the catchword pull toward the idol-makers' own failed witnesses is properly disclosed rather than resolved by merging.
items.evidence: A fresh title-stacked koh-amar opens the row, “This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: "I am the first, and I am the last” (web:Isa.44.6, byte tier at אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן), a different title pairing than the fear-not address before it, and closes at “I don't know any other Rock.” (web:Isa.44.8), immediately before the register shift into third-person idol-satire. The row's own witness language reaching toward the idol-makers' failed witnesses two verses later is disclosed as a live catchword pull rather than folded into either unit.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah single-witness (petuchah mark, Isa.44.5, neighbor)

items.claim: The unit's own opening boundary is argued from a register/person shift alone, with no koh-amar, hoy, massa, or addressee-shift signal marking it -- which the row's own text concedes -- and its device notes separately cross-reference a neighboring row's later field use.
items.evidence: The row itself states its opening cut is 'argued from this prose-inside-poetry register shift rather than from a koh-amar or fear-not frame,' and its own rejected-alternative sentence concedes 'no koh-amar or addressee marker opens Isa.44.9 on its own.' The third-person satire onset “Everyone who makes a carved image is vain.” (web:Isa.44.9, byte tier at יֹֽצְרֵי פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ) is a register/person shift from the preceding first-person divine self-declaration, and register/parallelism classes are never alone a valid boundary driver; the live rival that keeps the satire inside the trial speech as its own failed-witness evidence is therefore not clearly the weaker reading. Separately, the same row's device notes state that its ketiv/qere citation at Isa.44.24 (a verse entirely outside this unit's own span) 'covers the ketiv/qere note at that verse for the adjoining row's use of the same field,' which names the existence and field content of another row rather than stating this row's own grounds by content.
tier_citations: row-text self-disclosure (opening-boundary rationale and rejected alternative)

items.claim: The unit is warranted by a genuine addressee-shift back to direct second-person address after the satire's third-person register, and it correctly stops before the doxology rather than absorbing it, disclosing the shared redemption catchword instead of merging.
items.evidence: The address returns to direct exhortation at “Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant.” (web:Isa.44.21, byte tier at זְכָר אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי אָ֑תָּה), echoing the named-servant address of Isa.44.1-Isa.44.2, and closes at “Return to me, for I have redeemed you.” (web:Isa.44.22), immediately before the heavens' doxology opens at Isa.44.23 as its own unit. The shared redemption vocabulary reaching into that doxology is disclosed as a catchword pull rather than absorbed into this row's span.
